name: Dangme (Adangme)
notes: Dangme (Adangme, Adaŋgbi), a Ga-Dangme (Kwa) language of the Eastern Region and Greater Accra Region, Ghana, closely related to Ga. Latin script plus ɛ, ɔ, ŋ; tones are not normally written (Dangme has three tones: high, mid, low, with terracing). Seven oral vowels a e ɛ i o ɔ u, five nasal vowels written with a following ⟨n⟩ (not modelled as separate graphemes here). 23 consonant phonemes including the doubly-articulated labial-velars ⟨gb⟩ /ɡ͡b/, ⟨kp⟩ /k͡p/ and the labial-velar nasal ⟨ŋm⟩ /ŋ͡m/. ⟨j⟩ = /dʒ/ with fricative allophone [ʒ] for /j/ in some contexts, ⟨ts⟩ = /tʃ/, ⟨ny⟩ = /ɲ/, ⟨y⟩ = /j/. /l/ varies between a lateral approximant and a central trill/tap [r]. Syllable structure is (C)(C)V(C), where a second onset consonant is restricted to /l/.
